questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I spoke the language, knew the place from previous visits and was interested in the cultural aspects.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty hard - the webpage of Humboldt was not always up to date, people didn't respond in time and some information was received very late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is the person in charge of international students providing one information meeting. Not a lot of help but I knew I could contact here if I needed to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me fairly easy since i could take over a room from another danish girl who was a friend of a friend. Definitely recommend using your network and social media to gain reach - and reach out to anyone you know has some kind of connection to the place. Even though it's a far out connection and they don't necessarily know anything or anyone directly, but they might put you into contact with someone who can help.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it's a great way to meet other people who are either natives or not, but don't have anything with the uni-world to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Related to Berlin and probably most other European capitals; housing is tough at the moment, it's pricy and you need to be very lucky to find something that is affordable and centered. Be aware that you probably end up paying a lot for not that much

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hate the beaurocratic process, it takes such a long time and you receive different kinds of information depending on who you ask

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is both an electronic and physical part that can seem very confusing. The electronic is pretty straightforward but you also need to show up physically with some letters you have received for you to even get your student id.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was easier showing up at the information desk and ask for help, then they showed you in the right direction/were helpful with who you needed to contact

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all the classes I wanted so that was great

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That you can sign up for as many classes as you want even if exceeds the 30 credits. So be respectful but choose all the courses you find interesting

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the courses were very interesting and cool, one was trash

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: One course was literally almost kindergarten level. I know it was a course aimed at Erasmus students both on their master and bachelor but the level wasn't adequate for either - you could have taken it in primary school. The courses I took that were for MA students only were great; they were engaging, interesting and taught me a lot

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had one course for 2 credits which was only lectures and the exam was a written comment for three of the 15 lectures, so that differed quite a lot from the usual teaching style. The other courses were without an actual lecture but only a seminar so that required you to be more engaged which i thought was great.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Anthropology of the Senses: Urban Soundscapes
Be your own Berlin: Urban Performance in Tourism 
Institutskolluqium: Other Waves in Anthropology 
Quantitative Text Analysis

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All but Be your own Berlin. The series of lectures were interesting since they were at the department of Anthropology and allowed students to listen to research within different fields. The Quantitative Text Analysis was interesting because you learned to analyse large text corpora in R but also required you to have a good understanding of coding beforehand or at least a very strong interest to learn, since not much help was offered coding wise. And the Urban Soundscapes one I would recommend if you are interested in the concept of noise and sounds and want tools to analyse this (or other concepts)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't join any but heard that the uni-sport thing was good and cheap

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports i think, don't know what else

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Museums, clubs, bars, caffees

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going clubbing, meet a lot of great people there. And go explore the different neighbourhoods

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, Berlin is not very different from Copenhagen

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Easier to socialize with the students you have courses with, so maybe don't only aim for Erasmus or English speaking courses (of course requires you to know the language pretty well before hand)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Germans can be stiff and kinda awkward but that's also a bit funny

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People in Berlin are very open minded which is great

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Mensa is great and extremely cheap, bring tupperware

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask around as much as possible

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The cultural and social part. I didn't work here and the semester has definitely been the most relaxed semester ever, allowing me to socialize a lot

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning learning to do stuff alone if you don't know anyone here and getting out of your comfort zone

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun :D

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
